## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is exactly one reentrancy class assigned to each of the 7 new symbols, with none left unclassified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008] — PASS: FR-008 enumerates all 7: `fixpp_dict_load_from_xml` → SINGLE_THREAD; `fixpp_dict_destroy` → THREAD_SAFE; `fixpp_session_config_set_tcp_endpoint` → SINGLE_THREAD; `fixpp_session_config_set_reset_seqnum_policy` → SINGLE_THREAD; `fixpp_session_acceptor_bound_endpoint` → THREAD_SAFE; `fixpp_msg_field_count` → REQUIRES_SESSION_LOCK; `fixpp_msg_field_at` → REQUIRES_SESSION_LOCK. 7/7 classified, none unclassified.
- [x] CHK002 Is the "caller serializes concurrent access to the SAME clone handle" obligation stated as an explicit requirement, not left implicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008] — PASS: FR-008 explicitly states "with the caller serializing concurrent access to the *same* clone handle" as the condition under which the runtime THREAD_SAFE clone guarantee holds; also in contracts/field-iteration.md clone-handle reentrancy note.
- [x] CHK003 Are the two mandatory concurrency witnesses (TSan concurrent-double-destroy on the same dict handle; clone cross-strand off-strand read) both specified as required? [Completeness, Spec §SC-003/SC-004] — PASS: SC-004 specifies "A TSan concurrent-double-destroy witness (two threads racing `fixpp_dict_destroy` on the same handle) confirms no data race on `tag_`/the `shared_ptr` and exactly-once teardown"; SC-003 specifies "A clone-iteration cross-strand witness iterates a detached 051 clone off the session strand (a different thread, after the source dispatch window closed)".
- [x] CHK004 Is the consumer obligation for the single-thread config setters (`set_tcp_endpoint`, `set_reset_seqnum_policy`) — i.e. not called concurrently on the same cfg — documented? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008] — PASS: Both symbols carry `FIXPP_SINGLE_THREAD` per FR-008; `[2i §4.10]` (incorporated by reference) defines SINGLE_THREAD as "the caller MUST ensure no concurrent invocation against the same handle"; contracts/transport-endpoint.md states "Reentrancy: SINGLE_THREAD (a session-config setter, per the existing `fixpp_session_config_set_*` family)" for both symbols.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK005 Is the `fixpp_dict_destroy` THREAD_SAFE requirement specified with the EXACT critical-section boundary — `{check tag_ != DEAD, release shared_ptr, rewrite tag_ = DEAD, registry insert}` as ONE atomic unit, not a registry-only lock? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002/FR-008] — PASS: FR-002 states "a process-global mutex MUST cover the entire critical section as one atomic unit — `{ check tag_ != DEAD, release the shared_ptr ref, rewrite tag_ = DEAD, insert into the bounded dead-shell registry }` — NOT merely the registry insert"; FR-008 echoes the same boundary. Also in data-model.md E-1 and contracts/dictionary-loader.md.
- [x] CHK006 Is it explicitly stated WHICH data is raced (the non-atomic `tag_` + `shared_ptr` sitting OUTSIDE the registry) so the full-critical-section scope is justified, not arbitrary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002/FR-008] — PASS: FR-002 names "the race is on the non-atomic `tag_` + `shared_ptr`, which sit OUTSIDE the registry"; FR-008 echoes "the race is on the non-atomic `tag_`/`shared_ptr` outside the registry". The justification for the wider lock scope is explicit.
- [x] CHK007 Is the not-yet-bound semantics of `acceptor_bound_endpoint` (`*port_out = 0` + `FIXPP_ERR_OK`, pollable) specified clearly enough to be a thread-safe poll contract? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005] — PASS: FR-005 states "a not-yet-bound session yields `*port_out = 0` with `FIXPP_ERR_OK` so the consumer can poll"; Edge Cases confirms "not-yet-bound (port 0); the consumer polls"; contracts/transport-endpoint.md: "a session not yet bound yields *port_out = 0 with FIXPP_ERR_OK (poll until non-zero)". THREAD_SAFE annotation makes this a thread-safe poll contract.
- [x] CHK008 Is the decision that the static `check_capi_reentrancy.sh` gate stays one-annotation-per-symbol (and `[2i §4.6]` is NOT edited) stated so a reviewer does not expect a gate change? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008] — PASS: FR-008 closes with "The static `check_capi_reentrancy.sh` gate checks one annotation per declaration and cannot distinguish an inbound-flyweight read from a clone read on the same shared symbol, so the gate stays unchanged and `[2i §4.6]` is NOT edited." Reviewer has explicit confirmation.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK014 Conflict check: does the runtime-THREAD_SAFE clone guarantee conflict with the static REQUIRES_SESSION_LOCK in any consumer-visible way that the spec must disambiguate (which lifetime/thread rule a binding author follows for inbound vs clone)? [Conflict, Spec §FR-008] — PASS: No conflict; spec disambiguates by handle-state. REQUIRES_SESSION_LOCK governs inbound flyweight reads (inside the dispatch window, on the session strand); runtime THREAD_SAFE governs detached 051 clone handles (owner-controlled lifetime, session-independent). FR-008 and contracts/field-iteration.md both explain the two regimes explicitly. A binding author follows REQUIRES_SESSION_LOCK inside dispatch callbacks, and THREAD_SAFE (with same-handle serialization) for clone handles after detach.
- [x] CHK015 Is the bounded dead-shell retention under the destroy lock specified so a reviewer can confirm it does not unbounded-grow under concurrent destroys? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002] — PASS: FR-002 states "retains a bounded dead shell (dicts are O(few) per process — a binding loads a handful — so engine-style retention is bounded)"; data-model.md E-1 and contracts/dictionary-loader.md both echo "dicts are O(few) → bounded". The bound is justified by the usage pattern (dictionaries are loaded once at startup, not per-message), consistent with the engine-destroy precedent.
